title: What Is Sin?
subtitle: Wrongdoing, responsibility, and why repentance is more than feeling guilty
summary: Islam treats sin as wrongdoing before the Creator, not a guilt inherited at birth or just a breach of social custom. It distinguishes how grave an act is from how fully its doer is to blame. It also warns against pride and offers repentance as a real return to God. This helps explain both harm to others and duties toward Him.

seo.metaTitle: What Is Sin? Islam and Christianity Compared
seo.metaDescription: What makes an act sinful? Islam's account of wrongdoing, moral responsibility, degrees of sin, and the hope of sincere repentance.

sections.title: A Real Wrong, Not a Worthless Person
sections.body:
Islam treats sin as a real wrong that must be faced and changed, not proof that a person is worthless. An act can harm someone else's rights, damage character, or break a duty toward the Creator.

Both truths matter: the act was wrong, and a way back to God remains open. The Quran holds them together.

sections.title: More Than Getting Caught
sections.body:
A lie can remain wrong even when it succeeds. Neglect can betray a duty even when no law punishes it. Calling something sin places conduct before a standard beyond ease, reputation, or a group's approval.

Islam finds that standard in God's wisdom and guidance. This does not make every cultural habit sacred or every charge of sin correct. A rule's claim to come from God still needs evidence and a careful reading.

sections.title: Does Sin Require a Responsible Choice?
sections.body:
Islam does not start by assigning a child Adam's guilt. Quran 17:15 places the burden of wrongdoing with its doer and also links punishment with the sending of a messenger.

Knowing what someone did is not the same as knowing how fully that person is to blame. Knowledge, intent, careless neglect, and the setting all matter. This calls for care in judging people. It does not mean an act cannot be wrong.

sections.title: Why Degrees of Wrongdoing Matter
sections.body:
Treating a passing fault and deliberate cruelty as the same fails to take harm seriously. The Quran distinguishes major sins from lesser faults in 4:31 and 53:32.

Christians also recognize degrees of sin. The [Catholic distinction between mortal and venial sin](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_three/section_one/chapter_one/article_8/iv_the_gravity_of_sin_mortal_and_venial_sin.html), for example, considers how grave an act is, what the person knew, and what they freely chose. This is a Catholic way of judging sin, not the Islamic categories under new names.

sections.title: Facing Wrong Without Claiming to Be Pure
sections.body:
Quran 4:31 and 53:32 give grounds for hope while taking grave wrongdoing seriously. The latter also warns against declaring oneself pure. Noticing someone else's fault does not put anyone beyond failure.

Quran 66:8 calls for sincere repentance. Quran 3:135 describes people who seek forgiveness after wrongdoing and do not knowingly persist. The aim is neither denial nor endless self-blame, but an honest change of course.

sections.title: A Real Point of Contact With Christianity
sections.body:
Romans 3:23 recognizes widespread human failure. 1 John 3:4 links sin with lawlessness, while 1 John 1:9 connects confession with forgiveness and cleansing. These texts do not support the claim that Christian faith makes wrongdoing unimportant.

Romans 6:23 places the Christian remedy in God's gift through Christ. [What Is Salvation?](/articles/what-is-salvation) examines why Islam understands the remedy differently. The question here is what a person needs to recognize and turn away from.

sections.title: An Objection: Why Count a Private Act as Sin?
sections.body:
Some wrongs are clear because someone is hurt. Others concern worship, gratitude, or conduct whose effects are less direct. Why should neglecting God count as wrong if there is no human victim?

Islam answers that duties go beyond visible injury. Gratitude can be owed to a giver even when a lack of gratitude cannot harm that giver. If the Creator gives and sustains life, refusing every duty toward Him is not an empty choice. This argument needs a real Creator and genuine guidance from Him. A religious command with no supporting grounds cannot prove its own authority.

sections.title: Avoiding Both Constant Fear and Carelessness
sections.body:
Degrees of sin are not an excuse to nurture lesser wrongs. Repeated dishonesty can harm a relationship even when each lie seems small.

Nor does every unwanted thought, anxious feeling, or doubt justify a sweeping verdict against a person. A beginner needs sound guidance about real duties, not a habit of treating every fear as God's judgment. Hard cases call for a qualified teacher, not a rule invented to fit the fear.

sections.title: Naming the Wrong Makes Repair Possible
sections.body:
Islam gives moral failure a direction: name the wrong without making it a fixed identity. A dishonest deal calls for honesty and repair, not just an unrelated religious act. A neglected duty toward God calls for renewed worship.

The invitation joins duty with hope. Guilt can be admitted without becoming the whole truth about a person.

sections.title: The Next Question Is How to Return
sections.body:
[Sin and Repentance](/articles/sin-and-repentance) explains how to stop harm, seek forgiveness, and rebuild conduct. [Original Sin vs Personal Responsibility](/articles/original-sin-vs-personal-responsibility) addresses the separate question of the human starting point.

For someone still weighing a religion's authority, [What Is Revelation?](/articles/what-is-revelation) explains why a command needs more than a speaker's claim that it comes from God.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does Islam teach that all sins are equally serious?
A: No. Quran 4:31 and 53:32 distinguish grave wrongdoing from lesser faults, while warning against pride and knowingly carrying on in sin.

Q: Does a person inherit someone else's guilt?
A: Islam rejects inherited guilt. Quran 17:15 keeps blame with the person responsible. Catholic, Orthodox, and Reformed Christians explain this question differently; the separate article on original sin examines those views.

Q: Does calling an act sinful settle a person's final fate?
A: No. Naming a wrong is not the same as knowing a person's full intent, circumstances, repentance, or standing before God.

Q: Is repentance just feeling bad?
A: No. Quran 3:135 and 66:8 connect a sincere return with turning away from wrongdoing. When another person's rights were harmed, repentance also calls for repair.

sections.title: Sources and Further Reading
sections.body:
The selected Quran passages establish personal accountability, differing degrees of sin, and sincere return. The Bible cards show both moral seriousness and the Christian account of grace.

The linked Catholic source describes one church's classification of sin. The works below provide Islamic ethical guidance and wider Christian theological context.

quranVerses.arabic: مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِن تَجْتَنِبُوا۟ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُم مُّدْخَلًۭا كَرِيمًۭا
quranVerses.translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance [into Paradise].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ ۚ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌۭ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ ۖ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
quranVerses.translation: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوْبَةًۭ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَٰحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُوا۟ لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَن يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُوا۟ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

furtherReading.author: Imam al-Nawawi
furtherReading.note: The chapter on repentance explains moral return and the significance of other people's rights.
